traps: `cargo nextest show-config default-config` does not exist in cargo-nextest 0.9.133; the only `show-config` subcommands are `version` and `test-groups`. To verify one of nextest's own defaults for the pinned version, grep the installed binary — `strings -n 6 $(which cargo-nextest) | grep leak-timeout` prints the embedded default-config values (confirmed `leak-timeout = "200ms"`). Do not take a default value on trust from documentation for another version.

`scripts/cargo-ci.sh` runs `incremental-preflight` (scripts/cargo-ci.sh:305) BEFORE paying for any compilation, and it fails when a non-empty `incremental` directory exists anywhere under the worktree's `target/`. cargo-ci sets `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` for its own steps, but any ad-hoc `cargo build`/`cargo test`/`cargo clippy`/`cargo nextest` run beforehand leaves `target/debug/incremental` behind and the gate then fails for that reason alone, with nothing wrong in the change. Remedy before every gate run: `rm -rf target/debug/incremental`, or pass `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` to every ad-hoc cargo invocation.

`scripts/cargo-ci.sh` takes a MACHINE-GLOBAL flock at `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/cargo-ci.lock` and holds it for the whole run (scripts/cargo-ci.sh:64-68), waiting up to `CARGO_CI_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (default 1800s) and exiting 75 on timeout. Gate runs across different worktrees therefore SERIALIZE: parallel waves parallelise authoring only, never gates. Do not launch more concurrent gate runs than can finish inside 1800s, or queued ones fail on lock timeout rather than on their own content. Cheapest correct pattern: gate once on merged `main`, where `target/` is warm, and let `jit gate evaluate` reuse that verdict for every issue sharing the same content.

The stale-binary guard blocks EVERY `jit gate evaluate` once HEAD moves ahead of the installed binary's build commit: exit 10, 'this jit binary predates the tree under review'. Any commit touching `crates/jit/**` triggers it, so it recurs throughout this epic. Remedy: `./scripts/install-jit.sh` (never a bare `cargo install`, which loses the provenance the guard reads), then confirm with `jit --version` that the reported commit matches HEAD. Reinstall AFTER the last commit of a merge batch and BEFORE evaluating gates, or the reinstall is itself immediately stale.
Two gate runs redirecting to the same log path clobber each other's evidence, and the surviving file looks like one coherent run. Give every gate run its own log file name.

A backgrounded gate run SURVIVES stopping the agent that launched it, keeps the global cargo-ci flock, and blocks later runs while still writing to its original log path. After stopping any agent, check for orphans holding the lock (`fuser -v /tmp/cargo-ci.lock`, then `readlink /proc/<pid>/cwd`) before launching a replacement.

A new issue created mid-epic with no dependency edges makes whole-repo `jit validate` exit 4 ('isolated issue not connected to the dependency graph'), which fails the epic's own `repo-validate` gate. Wire every issue created during execution into the DAG when you create it.

`/tmp` on this host is a ~16 GiB tmpfs, and earlier sessions of this epic left about 12 GiB of scratch in it (per-issue cargo target dirs `/tmp/jit-<short-id>-target`, seven finished worktrees, benchmark helper targets). When it fills, the suite fails for reasons that look like product defects — a whole-workspace run showed 57 doctest failures and CLI exit-code failures — and the agent's own shell stops capturing command output (writes fail with EDQUOT, `echo` returns exit 1 with no output). Check `stat -f -c '%a' /tmp` before trusting any measurement or gate result, and reclaim worktrees per wave as the protocol requires. Every warm number recorded before session 6 (60,562-113,272 ms) was measured under this pressure and is not comparable to a clean-host measurement.

The first warm suite run after any change that invalidates the nextest setup-script fixture caches costs about 26 s extra: a cold-cache `cargo nextest run -p jit --lib` measured 41.4 s against 15.1 s warm on the same tree. Discard the first run after such a change; measuring it as if it were warm reads as a large regression that does not exist.

A raw-JSON journal fixture asserting only `.is_err()` can pass for the wrong reason: a fixture with a placeholder `layout_digest` is refused by the layout check before any version or field check runs, so it proves nothing about the boundary under test. Build the fixture from a real interrupted transaction and mutate only the field whose boundary you are testing, then prove the test fails when that boundary is reverted.

created_during_execution.title: Stop pinning the live dogfood package identity hash to a literal
created_during_execution.why: `main` was already red at epic start, independent of this epic: `test_shipped_package_decodes_without_edits_and_preserves_identity_hash` pinned the LIVE dogfood profile package's identity hash to a literal, and that profile packages this repository's own config (including contrib/gates prompts) as assets, so an earlier prompt edit moved the hash. Every cargo-ci gate in all seven waves would have failed on it. The invoker judged the test wrong and the commit right. Fixed on main as d2c8693b by keeping the independent recomputation of the released v1 identity algorithm and dropping the literal; synthetic-fixture literals kept. Wired as a dependency of the epic so whole-repo validation passes.

created_during_execution.title: Bind profile fixture cache roots to runtime artifacts

created_during_execution.title: Screen an optimized ordinary JIT library artifact
created_during_execution.why: The prior ordinary library-plus-binary wrapper missed its clean-build ceiling by 4.59 percentage points. Restricting optimization to the ordinary library recovered nearly all of that build margin, but its representative rebuild still missed the hard 25% ceiling by 437 ms, so runtime was correctly not sampled and the integration was reverted with reviewed evidence.

delegation_model: Set by the invoker in session 6, superseding the earlier codex-only model: hard tasks go to native Opus subagents dispatched with the Agent tool, moderate tasks go to native Sonnet subagents, and easy tasks go to `codex exec -m gpt-5.6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort=high`. gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-5.6-terra are no longer permitted. The lead reviews every diff, runs configured gates, and owns integration. When a codex worker must run the test suite, pass `-c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true`, or the three `commands::serve::tests` listener tests fail with `Operation not permitted` and nextest cancels the run.
gate_cost_model: Measured this session on this host: a cold worktree cargo-ci run is 10+ minutes; a warm run on main is ~3-5 minutes; each `code-review` run is 3-5 minutes and is per-issue (no reuse). cargo-ci verdicts DO reuse across issues over identical content, so merge a whole wave, then evaluate cargo-ci per issue for one execution plus reuses. Worker cargo-ci runs in fresh worktrees are the single largest avoidable cost: from wave 2 on, have workers verify with focused tests plus fmt and clippy only, and let the lead's post-merge gate on warm main be the authoritative run.

escalations.summary: Invoker approved nextest-level stale-fixture preparation plus shared immutable profile/repair fixture support on 2026-08-12; dispatched as hard leaves 1fc8fec3 and 4731256d.

escalations.resolution: The invoker restored local Codex CLI authentication before session 6. The unchanged code-review gate then passed on the first attempt with zero findings, and b883f916 completed.
escalations.summary: The configured code-review checker invokes the local Codex CLI, whose OAuth access and refresh tokens remain revoked. Across three consecutive goal turns, cached status and even one minimal echo request gave misleading positive signals, while every configured gate attempt and exact-session resume reproduced HTTP 401 token_revoked/refresh_token_invalidated. The human must log out and sign in again before required AI review gates can run.

surfaced_pitfalls: A merged issue's cargo-ci can fail on a different in-progress issue already present on main. Run 4b75ba0b for 4aa15137 reproduced 47836e2e's deterministic 5/6 nextest observation defect while the recovery-seam focused tests, fmt, and clippy were green. Preserve the failed run as shared-branch evidence; do not charge rework to the unaffected issue, and rerun after the owning fix lands.

A direct workspace nextest run can fail merged_tree_gate_verification_tests because its nested cargo-ci self-test enables a host sccache path that passes inside the outer cargo-ci gate but fails when invoked standalone. The warm profiler sets CARGO_CI_NO_SCCACHE=1 for both runs; per-test exec_time excludes compilation, and the profiler self-test asserts the isolation. Do not weaken the producer with --no-fail-fast or publish partial evidence.

Do not wire --test-suite-ms into cargo-ci before reducing warm suite work. A complete run measured 113,272 ms and a separate warm incomplete span already measured 60,562 ms; the unchanged checker correctly rejects both against 30,000 ms. The 883,556 ms aggregate profile also has a 42,139 ms perfect-packing lower bound after doctests on 24 logical CPUs, proving this is not just scheduler noise.

A test-support cache root derived from env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR) is not stable when Cargo reuses setup and test artifacts compiled from different worktrees. Gate 9b87eafe failed because the setup receipt and consumer inferred different target roots. Derive the cache context from each canonical runtime artifact layout and validate the receipt entry against the independently derived consumer root.

Do not accept benchmark validators that compare captured compiler paths to the validator's current checkout. The b883f916 validator passed in its worker worktree but failed immediately after merge on main. Bind and corroborate the recorded audit checkout root, then validate exact joined paths without requiring that historical path to still exist.

A clean-build sample that barely passes a build ceiling does not authorize retention by itself. The b883f916 clean screen passed by only 122 ms, but its mandatory representative rebuild failed by 437 ms; preserve both and stop before runtime as the contract requires.

If an automatic AI review returns 'Agent produced no output' in a few seconds, inspect the provider session before retrying repeatedly. For b883f916, direct resume showed HTTP 401 token_revoked and refresh_token_invalidated; repository rework cannot fix that external authentication state.

Do not treat `codex login status` as proof that the OAuth session is usable. It reported `Logged in using ChatGPT` while fresh model and websocket requests still returned token_revoked and refresh_token_invalidated. A real `codex logout` followed by `codex login` is required.

Do not use a trivial requested echo as the sole authentication proof. One low-effort `codex exec` printed `AUTH_OK` after multiple 401 errors, but the configured high-effort review and exact session resume still failed with revoked tokens. The gate itself must complete successfully.
